summary: @servicetitan/toolbelt-shared-registry 1.14.3 preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute a bundled obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs". setup.mjs is variable-name-obfuscated and, at install time, detects the host platform and libc (glibc vs musl), downloads a Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, extracts the bun binary to a temporary directory, chmods it 0755, and execFileSyncs it against the sibling file math_init.js shipped in the tarball. math_init.js is a ~728KB Bun-bundled artifact (leading `// @bun @bun-cjs` marker) consisting of a shuffled string array and a lookup decoder (WV8StW rotates the array; hc1jfK9 maps characters through a scrambled alphabet), with randomized identifiers, no corresponding source in src/, no documentation, and no reference from dist/index.js. The advertised library code in dist/ is a small React/IOC registry helper and does not require a second language runtime. Pulling the Bun runtime specifically to execute an opaque payload that Node-based tooling cannot inspect gives whoever published this version host-level code execution on any developer machine or CI runner that runs npm install. The package is published under the @servicetitan scope with plausible ServiceTitan-adjacent metadata (peerDependencies on @servicetitan/react-ioc and @servicetitan/web-components), while all hostile behavior is confined to setup.mjs + math_init.js and is unrelated to the advertised registry functionality — consistent with a compromised-maintainer or scope-impersonation scenario.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
